subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should this RFC remain the umbrella for multi-session architecture, or should maintainers split it into narrower canonical issues such as topic-session families, WebUI lifecycle, routing fixes, and shared-memory security?
rationale: Current main partially implements the requested primitives, but the remaining work changes product architecture and security boundaries rather than a narrow broken code path.

options.title: Split into staged design issues
options.body: Keep the discussion open until maintainers choose canonical sub-issues for routing identity, WebUI session lifecycle, topic-family semantics, and shared-memory security.

options.title: Make topic families canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90916 as the canonical state-model issue and move only the missing routing/UI/security leftovers there.

options.title: Approve broad rewrite
options.body: Sponsor a coordinated architecture change across routing, storage, UI, and memory with explicit migration and security review before any implementation PR.

recommendation.title: Split into staged design issues
recommendation.body: Keep the discussion open until maintainers choose canonical sub-issues for routing identity, WebUI session lifecycle, topic-family semantics, and shared-memory security.

likelyOwner.reason: The routing/session-key and session-store history is strongest around Peter Steinberger, and the decision crosses core architecture rather than a plugin-only surface.
